blockers.title: On the account's other phone, an erased course's personal data stays in the raw database storage after the server erase reaches it
blockers.evidence: The device that runs the erase compacts afterwards (courses.ts eraseAllCourseData -> compactEmptyCourseDatabase), and its raw IndexedDB blocks hold no trace of the course. A second phone loses the course through the sync stream instead: src/App.tsx:941-953 reloads it, and src/persistence/migrations.ts:147-157 drops only uploadRefusals. Neither path runs VACUUM or marks a compaction as pending. Live run against the development backend with two browser contexts on test account 1 and a synthetic student 'Zebedeo'. Phone B's queries come back empty: students 0, ps_oplog 0, ps_untyped 0, uploadRefusals 0, ps_crud 0, PRAGMA freelist_count 0. A raw scan of phone B's IndexedDB ('cvc-helper.db') still finds 'Zebedeo' after the removal, and again after a further reopen. The same scan on phone A finds nothing. The deleted bytes sit as unused space inside live pages, which only a VACUUM rewrites. The repository's own standard (UG3 SP-UG3-1, the erase's compaction) treats this as readable data.
blockers.reproduction: Throwaway spec in my scratchpad, run twice with the same result. (1) Context A: create an offline course, add student 'Zebedeo', signInForTests(user 1), startBackup, reload, and poll the server until the student is there. (2) Context B: empty device, signInForTests(user 1), startBackup -> reopen, reload, and wait for the course heading. B's raw IndexedDB scan finds 'Zebedeo'. (3) A erases through Impostazioni > Elimina il corso; the server's course count reaches 0. (4) B reloads itself to 'Crea il corso'. B's raw scan still finds 'Zebedeo', also after another reload. The account was cleared afterwards (courses 0, students 0).
blockers.specRef: 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md B6 success predicate ('nothing of the removed course remains readable on the server or the device'); AGENTS.md §17

importantFindings.title: After an offline erase, Esci and a signed-out full reset silently discard the only pending server erase; the erase confirmation promises it unconditionally
importantFindings.evidence: CourseErase.tsx:93 adds 'e dal backup online, appena c’è connessione' whenever the device is synced, including after Esci or under another account; the erase actually completes only when this account signs in again on this device. After an offline erase, the ps_crud-based Esci question (OnlineBackup.tsx:579-581) mentions only ordinary pending changes and says nothing about the pending course erase. Once signed out, the full reset (CourseFiles.tsx:667) says 'La copia nel backup online resta: per eliminarla accedi al backup ed elimina il corso', although the course is no longer on the device to erase. The reset then deletes serverErasures.
importantFindings.reproduction: Fake-backend scratch spec: back up a course with a synthetic student, take the backend offline (navigator.onLine false, routes aborted), Elimina il corso, create a new course, then Esci. The question read 'Uscire? 1 modifica non è ancora online…' (the new course's insert). serverErasures still held the erased id. Azzera tutti i dati locali showed the 'copia … resta' text and reset. The fake server still held the erased course and its student (courses 1, students 1), and nothing remained on the device to finish the erase.
importantFindings.specRef: 01_PRODUCT_SPEC.md §Settings (erase 'backup copy too'); owner decision 18; B6 checklist 'an erase offline and never reconnected'

importantFindings.title: SP-B4-3 is resolved only for the whole-course erase; deleting one person's data still depends on device clocks
importantFindings.evidence: settleServerErasures (session.ts) deletes the course row unconditionally and lets the cascade remove its rows, so no clock is involved; the code confirms this and b6-erase.spec.ts confirms the request carries only an id filter. A single student delete still goes through the B4 rule (DELETE where updatedAt <= the value the device saw), and an older or clock-ahead edit from another phone can bring the row back. Decision 19 and 03 §3 record this as decision 16's accepted gap until 1.0.0.
importantFindings.reproduction: By construction; see placementConvergence.test.ts, the expected failure cited in decision 16.
importantFindings.specRef: 04 B6 adversarial checklist (SP-B4-3); owner decisions 16 and 19

importantFindings.title: The tombstone that refuses another phone's late upload is not installed on the development backend
importantFindings.evidence: erased_courses answers 404 (the live spec's 'installed' branch did not run). Until supabase/migrations/20261028000000_course_erase.sql runs, the fallback is the delete alone, and another phone's whole-row upsert of the course row recreates it. The CVERA refusal is proven only against the fake backend. Records settled before the migration are forgotten (forgetServerErasures runs when installed=false), so the courses they cover never get a tombstone.
importantFindings.reproduction: Live spec run: 2 passed, with the CVERA assertion skipped because erased_courses answers 404.

qolFindings.title: In the backup's 'error' state the full reset text contradicts what the reset then does
qolFindings.evidence: FullReset's signedIn (CourseFiles.tsx:590-593) leaves out 'error', so it shows 'La copia nel backup online resta…'. eraseOnlineCopyBeforeReset (session.ts:356) includes 'error', tries the online erase, fails and refuses the reset.
qolFindings.reproduction: Fake backend unreachable with navigator.onLine true: the confirmation shows 'La copia … resta', and the reset is then refused with the 'nulla è stato azzerato' alert.

qolFindings.title: The retention text claims more than is verified and leaves out some places that keep data
qolFindings.evidence: erasure.ts states a flat 'al massimo 7 giorni'. The development backend runs on Supabase's Free plan, which publishes no retention (decision 17 says so), and PowerSync Cloud's daily compaction is asserted without a cited source. The text does not mention that the account's other phones keep their copy until they connect (and, per SP-B6-1, raw remnants afterwards), or that Postgres/API logs may keep refused rows' error details.
qolFindings.specRef: 04 B6 'states what the provider's backups keep and for how long'

qolFindings.title: An app below the server's minimum writer cannot erase online, and the message blames the connection
qolFindings.evidence: refuse_outdated_writer is a statement-level BEFORE DELETE trigger, so the course delete answers CVOLD. settleServerErasures returns false, and the backup then reports 'Backup non raggiungibile' and the reset says 'Riprova con la connessione'.
